rationale: The committee must choose among approaches that were studied in different ways and settings. A narrative review organised by where the loop breaks can compare them honestly without pooling incomparable completion figures (c1, c2), and can show who each approach misses (c3, c4). The national benchmark suggested as a lead is unverified and is not used.
alternatives: Systematic review with meta-analysis (refused: completion figures use different windows and denominators, and it cannot finish by January 2027)
Adopt structured report codes now and review later (refused: codes alone notify no one)
Rely on the structured review of failure points alone (refused: it does not compare approaches or their completion)
guidelines: SANRA items as a quality checklist for narrative reviews
whyNotMoreComplex: A systematic review with pooling would average figures that measure different things; the narrative review keeps each figure with its definition and setting, which is what the committee needs to compare approaches.

decision.statement: Conduct the narrative review of how health systems track follow-up of incidental imaging findings, covering every tracking approach, organised by where the loop breaks, with completion reported alongside each study's design and definitions, and separately for patients without a primary care clinician and emergency-only patients.
decision.question: Which tracking approaches should the narrative review cover, and how should it present them to the committee?

criteria.text: Published tracking approaches report different completion gains in different settings, so a structured comparison can inform the choice.
Failure points and inequities are described in the retrieved records and can be mapped to each approach.
A current review already compares tracking approaches across this mix of findings.

gates.requirement: Department chair approval of the review and librarian time
gates.evidence: Chair's email of 2026-09-08 assigning the librarian for three days, supplied by the investigator

gates.requirement: Quality committee agenda time on 14 January 2027
gates.evidence: Committee meeting of 14 January 2027 to choose a tracking approach, stated in the investigator's local facts

alternatives: Adopt structured report codes now and review later
Rely on the structured review of failure points alone
decision.note: Rests on ledger claims c1 to c4 from retrieved records; the unverified benchmark lead is excluded.

summary: Narrative review of all approaches recommended; the decision rests on four ledger claims and both gates are met.
